intent: Build configured-provider images without private credentials while validating runtime startup and Auth.js operations; preserve mode/session behavior and gate publication on faithful smoke checks.

evidence: Dockerfile:41-43: `ARG AUTH_MODE` / `ENV AUTH_MODE=$AUTH_MODE`; provider issuer/client ID are builder-only at lines 25-32.

next.config.ts:32-34 freezes browser provider availability and issuer, while lib/auth-mode.ts:22-38 reads runtime settings and lib/env.ts:33 permits optional anonymous startup. instrumentation.ts:3-15 has no parity guard.
scripts/verify-auth-image.sh:21-23 supplies the same public settings at runtime, so its positive configuration assertion does not exercise missing or mismatched runtime settings.

Reproduction on reviewed a365aa8d image ontokit/d03-web:optional-configured (81a85a5aa31c), Node 22.23.2, network none: optional mode with both synthetic secrets but no runtime issuer/client ID returned HTTP 200 {} from /api/auth/providers, despite compiled NEXT_PUBLIC_ZITADEL_CONFIGURED=true and issuer=https://identity.example.invalid. The temporary container was removed.
findings.first_evidence: Dockerfile:41-43: `ARG AUTH_MODE` / `ENV AUTH_MODE=$AUTH_MODE`; provider issuer/client ID are builder-only at lines 25-32.
findings.suggested_fix: At Node startup compare the compiled public auth mode, provider availability and issuer with the runtime effective mode/provider/issuer; reject mismatches with the existing generic startup marker. Keep a matching optional anonymous image valid, and preserve disabled mode when build and runtime match. Keep private credentials runtime-only; do not default a missing runtime public provider to anonymous for a configured image. Add network-isolated smoke cases for missing runtime issuer/client ID and mismatched issuer/mode, plus positive matching configured/anonymous cases. If comparing client ID too, retain nonsecret build metadata for that value without inventing a browser API contract.
findings.title: Configured image drifts: baked client flag vs unset runtime provider
findings.why_it_matters: An optional configured image can start healthy while advertising sign-in for a server with no provider. A different runtime issuer can also send sign-in to issuer B while browser logout targets baked issuer A. The existing green smoke tests inject matching values and miss this trigger.
findings.validation_reason: At reviewed a365aa8d, newly added Dockerfile:25–32 bakes provider identity into next.config.ts:32–34 browser flags without carrying it into the runner; when this optional/configured image is launched with both secrets but omitted runtime issuer/client ID, lib/env.ts:33 and lib/auth-mode.ts:22–38 accept anonymous configuration and auth.ts:43 returns no providers while lib/auth-mode.ts:47–50 still advertises sign-in, with no startup parity guard in instrumentation.ts:3–15; the supplied Node 22.23.2 network-isolated image reproduction exercised this exact precondition and observed HTTP 200 {} with compiled provider flag true, establishing the newly reachable R2 mismatch (live deployment incidence was not measured).
